Alger, 7 août 2026 (Aleria Tech) — Samsu: Algiers, August 7, 2026 (Aleria Tech) — Samsung unveils its new lineup of foldable smartphones for 2026, including a brand-new model, the Z Fold 8, and a revamped nomenclature. The Korean manufacturer is betting on a passport format to improve the user experience.
Samsung annonce une refonte de sa gamme: Samsung announces a revamp of its foldable smartphone lineup with the introduction of the Z Fold 8 and Z Flip 8, succeeding the Z Fold 7 and Z Flip 7 respectively. A new model, the Z Fold 8 Ultra, replaces the former Z Fold 7 at the top of the range. The nomenclature is evolving to align with that of the Galaxy S series, where the "Ultra" suffix designates the most advanced model. The Z Flip 8 FE, a budget-friendly version of the Z Flip 8, is also expected for the autumn.
Le changement vise à clarifier la hiérar: The change aims to clarify the product hierarchy, with the Z Fold 8 Ultra positioning itself as the highest-performing device in the Z family. Samsung justifies this decision by a desire for consistency with its other ranges, where the Ultra model embodies technological excellence.
Un format passeport pour le Z Fold 8: A passport format for the Z Fold 8
Le Z Fold 8 adopte un format inédit chez: The Z Fold 8 adopts a brand-new format for Samsung, inspired by competing models like the OPPO Find N (2021) or the Google Pixel Fold (2023). This design, described as a "passport" format, allows for better keyboard usability on the outer screen, overcoming the limitations of the traditional format. The foldable screen's aspect ratio is also optimized for viewing videos and movies.
Le constructeur coréen mise sur un écran: The Korean manufacturer is relying on a high-quality foldable screen with a nearly invisible crease and raw power bolstered by a silicon-carbon battery and 45W fast charging. However, water and dust resistance remains limited to IP54, and the model drops support for the S-Pen, sparking criticism among users.
Samsung prépare le terrain pour un évent: Samsung is preparing the ground for a potential foldable iPhone with a passport format, a persistent rumor in the industry. The South Korean group is counting on its technological lead to impose its standards before Apple's potential arrival. The Z Fold 8, weighing 201 grams and featuring reduced dimensions (81.9 × 123.9 mm), stands out for its compact format and versatility.
Les premiers retours soulignent un desig: Initial feedback highlights a polished design and pleasant handling, although the price remains a barrier for many consumers. Critics also point out high thermal throttling and a camera department deemed disappointing for a high-end device.
